roles.name: --feedback-danger
roles.purpose: an error message — a failed save, a field that will not take its value — as text

roles.name: --feedback-danger-border
roles.purpose: the border of an error callout

roles.name: --feedback-danger-muted
roles.purpose: an error callout's fill

roles.name: --feedback-info
roles.purpose: text of a neutral, informational callout — no outcome to signal, so it reads as page text

roles.name: --feedback-info-border
roles.purpose: the border of an informational callout

roles.name: --feedback-info-muted
roles.purpose: the fill of an informational callout — the recessed well

roles.name: --feedback-notice
roles.purpose: text of a notice the reader must not miss that is not a problem — the "new" badge's brand ink

roles.name: --feedback-notice-border
roles.purpose: the border of a notice callout

roles.name: --feedback-notice-muted
roles.purpose: the fill of a notice callout

roles.name: --feedback-success
roles.purpose: a confirmation that something worked, as text

roles.name: --feedback-success-border
roles.purpose: the border of a success callout

roles.name: --feedback-success-muted
roles.purpose: a success callout's fill

roles.name: --feedback-warning
roles.purpose: a caution about what just happened or is about to, as text

roles.name: --feedback-warning-border
roles.purpose: the border of a warning callout

roles.name: --feedback-warning-muted
roles.purpose: a warning callout's fill

roles.name: --gap-tight
roles.purpose: a title and its subline
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --icon-alert
roles.purpose: an alert's icon when the alert has no title

roles.name: --icon-alert-titled
roles.purpose: an alert's icon beside a title and its text — the same line weight, drawn larger

roles.name: --line-height-body
roles.purpose: prose, rows, labels and controls
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --radius-container
roles.purpose: a container that HOLDS content: a card, a dialog, a menu

roles.name: --size-alert-inset
roles.purpose: where an alert's text starts, clear of its icon: the alert's 12px side padding, the icon, a related gap. design-accepted — an alert is a compact banner inside a card, not a container of its own, so it keeps 12×8 rather than the container's 16 (Pete)
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --size-alert-inset-titled
roles.purpose: the same with a title, whose icon is larger
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --step-14
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-body
roles.purpose: running text, cells, hints, metadata
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-emphasis
roles.purpose: a column heading, a field error, a nav group, the status strip, a table footer
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-heading
roles.purpose: a card or section heading, a readout caption, a figure, initials
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: border-frame
roles.purpose: The two line roles — every border is one of them, by its job (design.md → Elevation & Depth). A frame (2px) is a container's edge and the splits and header bands between its sections. A line (1px) is a control's edge, an overlay's edge, and the rules between rows or items. Use these — never a numbered border width.

roles.name: type-body
roles.purpose: prose — descriptions, list text, dialog text
roles.value: font-size: var(--step-14); font-weight: var(--weight-body); line-height: var(--line-height-body)
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.
